Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our infra team dug into the draft topology and asked for a short written review focused on two items before we lock the purchase order:

1) Control plane egress requirements — we need a prescriptive list of outbound destinations and ports (for updates, telemetry, and licensing) and options for routing them through our transit firewall vs an explicit egress proxy.
2) Reference diagram that shows the demarcation between customer data plane, Redwood control plane, and logging/monitoring integrations (we run Splunk and an internal SIEM).

Can you send a single doc/diagram + short set of options (recommended, conservative, minimal) that we can use in our security review? Timing: procurement wants signoff by the end of next week.

Appreciate it —
Samir

Hi Samir —

Thanks, very reasonable asks. Attached is a first-pass reference diagram and a one-page egress matrix (priv-deploy-reference-diagram-v1.png, controlplane-egress-sequence-v1.pdf). TL;DR of the options below:

- Recommended (balanced): control plane egress through an authenticated egress proxy hosted in customer VPC, allowing outbound connections only to our service endpoints and telemetry.collect.redwood.com (443). Uses mutual TLS and IP allowlist. Retains customer-level auditability (split egress flow via VPC route table).
- Conservative (compliance-first): block direct outbound, route all control-plane traffic via customer-managed transit firewall with explicit port rules; require physical IP allowlist and customer-managed NAT. Adds operational overhead but minimal third-party exposure.
- Minimal (fast path): allow direct HTTPS egress from control-plane subnets to Redwood endpoints and the OS update repositories. Lower ops friction but increases third-party egress footprint.

Notes/assumptions:
- Control-plane agents only make outbound connections; data-plane (customer workloads) never egress to Redwood endpoints unless explicitly configured.
- Telemetry payloads are TLS and limited to metrics/traces/aggregated health pings; no raw customer payloads are included.
- For Splunk/SIEM forwarding we recommend a push model from customer side to their ingestion endpoint; if needed we can also support streaming via an encrypted forwarder into a customer-managed collector inside their VPC.

Suggested next steps: small sync with your infra/security to agree on ports and finalize the v1 diagram. I'm available tomorrow 10–11am PT or Wednesday 2–4pm PT.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple of technical clarifications from the runtime/serving side. Inline notes on the recommended vs conservative options: 

- Egress endpoints: in recommended mode the control-plane agent communicates with: api.redwood.ai:443 (control/config), telemetry.collect.redwood.com:443 (metrics), updater.redwood.ai:443 (binary/patch pulls). We can provide a CIDR list and stable hostname FQDNs; CIDRs are preferred for strict allowlists.
- mTLS: agents support mutual TLS using customer-provisioned client certs or Redwood-managed certs. For regulated customers we recommend customer-managed certs provisioned via KMS/HSM.
- Keepalive/idle: control-plane agents maintain short-lived connections with KV cache warmups; default keepalive interval 30s — ensure your FW allows ephemeral outbound high ports for TLS sessions.
- SIEM integration: rather than writing logs back to Redwood, we recommend exporting audit events to an S3 bucket in the customer account + cross-account role for Splunk ingestion. If that isn’t allowed, we can stream to a customer-managed collector inside the VPC over TLS.

Security redlines for conservative option: restrict outbound to only the three FQDNs above, enforce Source NAT only at the customer-managed NAT gateway (no internet gateway), and require certificate pinning verification on the agent. Those add procurement friction but close the risk surface.

I'll update the diagram with port-level annotations (443, 32768–65535 ephemeral) and an explicit route table snippet.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Can you publish the CIDR list for the endpoints (we need ranges for our firewall team)?
2) For the mTLS flow, does Redwood provide tooling to rotate certs automatically, or is that customer responsibility? We prefer automation where possible.
3) Can you propose a short runbook for “day-0 cutover” describing the sequence (DNS, NAT, egress proxy flip, smoke tests) — procurement wants a one-pager.

If you can get these items by EOD Thursday we can include them in the packet. Also please include any DoD for telemetry (what fields, retention, and whether any PII could be present).

Samir

Samir —

Attached is an updated diagram (priv-deploy-reference-diagram-v2.png) and a one-page cutover runbook draft. Quick answers to your follow-ups: 

1) CIDR list: attached in the design doc and mirrored below — we will provide a /24 set for each endpoint for allowlist stability (api.redwood.ai: 198.51.100.0/24, telemetry.collect.redwood.com: 198.51.101.0/24, updater.redwood.ai: 198.51.102.0/24). These are stable allocations for the next 12 months; any changes will be announced 30 days in advance.
2) Certificate rotation: Redwood supports automated cert rotation via our agent when customer opts into Redwood-managed certs; for customers that require customer-managed certs we provide a CLI tool and a templated automation playbook for rotation using KMS/HSM.
3) Day-0 cutover runbook: attached (cutover-runbook-onepager.pdf) — sequence is: (a) prepare and validate NAT/route tables, (b) stage egress proxy VM with our agent, (c) switch route table to point control-plane subnets at proxy, (d) run smoke tests (token fetch, health check, simple inference), (e) flip metrics export to customer SIEM collector. Estimated outage: 0–30s for in-flight connections; no data-plane interruption.

Telemetry DoD: metrics/traces (service health, request latency, token counts), no customer PII. Retention default 30d aggregated, 90d for raw traces in encrypted storage; we can extend per contract.

I've scheduled a 30-minute review with your security team for Friday 9:30am PT (invite sent). Action items we will deliver by EOD Thursday: CIDR list (done), cutover one-pager (attached), and a port-level route table snippet (included in the diagram).

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
